source.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
source.paraphrase: The method groups candidates by user-chosen behavior descriptors and retains strong examples across regions, revealing variety beyond a single overall winner.

research.mechanism_explanation: MAP-Elites motivates spreading search across descriptor-defined regions rather than repeatedly drawing from one global pool. The fixture exposes eligible rotation|feature streams, so this callback seeded-shuffles those pairs and yields one proposal from each active stream per round. It cannot see evaluation scores or maintain true per-cell elites; this is a coverage schedule, not a quality-selection method.
research.hypothesis: On each complete paired development run at four completed calls per arm, round-robin sampling from the eligible rotation×feature streams will reach more distinct valid cells than the synthetic uniform selector.
research.falsifier: Any complete matched development run with a unique_valid_cell_difference of zero or below falsifies the claimed per-run coverage gain. An incomplete comparison is untested, never counted as support.

human_review.summary: The development comparison completed four matched runs at four calls per arm. Challenger-minus-reference coverage differences were 0, 0, +1, and +2 cells; synthetic quality-pass differences were +1, -1, 0, and -1. The strict per-run coverage-gain hypothesis was falsified by the two zero-difference alpha runs; gains appeared only on beta. These are fixture-only observations.
human_review.rationale: The paper motivates preserving diversity across user-defined descriptors, but it does not predict that this callback will outperform a uniform selector. The callback can schedule fixture-provided streams but cannot observe candidate quality or select an elite for each cell, so the implementation tests breadth alone. The mixed outcome is descriptive; live performance, return correlation, and server acceptance remain unknown.
